chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you recognize the prolongation of affliction from its brevity?' We said: 'No.' He said: 'Whenever one of you is inspired to supplication during an affliction, then know that the affliction is short.'

key_terms.أُلْهِمَ: Was inspired (ulhima) — divine inspiration (ilham) implanted in the heart, distinct from wahy (prophetic revelation)
key_terms.بَلَاء: Affliction, trial, tribulation (bala') — a test from God, covering both hardships and blessings in classical usage
key_terms.دُعَاء: Supplication (du'a) — heartfelt personal prayer and invocation of God

ai.seo_question: How can you tell if an affliction will be short according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches his companions a divine sign by which one may discern whether an affliction will be short or prolonged: if God inspires a person to make du'a during the trial, this divine inspiration (ilham) is itself a mercy indicating that the affliction will be brief. The teaching is conveyed through a dialogue between the Imam and his companions, reflecting the pedagogical style of the Ahl al-Bayt. This hadith comes from Kitab al-Du'a in al-Kafi, in a chapter dedicated to the spiritual significance of being inspired toward supplication.
